Despite initially not wanting to add every feature under the sun to ripgrep,
over time, ripgrep has grown support for most features found in other file
searching tools. This includes searching for results spanning across multiple
lines, and opt-in support for PCRE2, which provides look-around and
backreference support.

At this point, the primary reasons not to use ripgrep probably consist of one
or more of the following:

* You need a portable and ubiquitous tool. While ripgrep works on Windows,
  macOS and Linux, it is not ubiquitous and it does not conform to any
  standard such as POSIX. The best tool for this job is good old grep.
* There still exists some other feature (or bug) not listed in this README that
  you rely on that's in another tool that isn't in ripgrep.
* There is a performance edge case where ripgrep doesn't do well where another
  tool does do well. (Please file a bug report!)
* ripgrep isn't possible to install on your machine or isn't available for your
  platform. (Please file a bug report!)


### Is it really faster than everything else?

Generally, yes. A large number of benchmarks with detailed analysis for each is
[available on my blog](https://blog.burntsushi.net/ripgrep/).

Summarizing, ripgrep is fast because:

* It is built on top of
  [Rust's regex engine](https://github.com/rust-lang/regex).
  Rust's regex engine uses finite automata, SIMD and aggressive literal
  optimizations to make searching very fast. (PCRE2 support can be opted into
  with the `-P/--pcre2` flag.)
* Rust's regex library maintains performance with full Unicode support by
  building UTF-8 decoding directly into its deterministic finite automaton
  engine.
* It supports searching with either memory maps or by searching incrementally
  with an intermediate buffer. The former is better for single files and the
  latter is better for large directories. ripgrep chooses the best searching
  strategy for you automatically.
* Applies your ignore patterns in `.gitignore` files using a
  [`RegexSet`](https://docs.rs/regex/1/regex/struct.RegexSet.html).
  That means a single file path can be matched against multiple glob patterns
  simultaneously.
* It uses a lock-free parallel recursive directory iterator, courtesy of
  [`crossbeam`](https://docs.rs/crossbeam) and
  [`ignore`](https://docs.rs/ignore).


### Feature comparison

Andy Lester, author of [ack](https://beyondgrep.com/), has published an
excellent table comparing the features of ack, ag, git-grep, GNU grep and
ripgrep: https://beyondgrep.com/feature-comparison/

Note that ripgrep has grown a few significant new features recently that
are not yet present in Andy's table. This includes, but is not limited to,
configuration files, passthru, support for searching compressed files,
multiline search and opt-in fancy regex support via PCRE2.

ripgrep (rg) recursively searches the current directory for lines matching
a regex pattern. By default, ripgrep will respect gitignore rules and
automatically skip hidden files/directories and binary files.

Use -h for short descriptions and --help for more details.

Project home page: https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep

USAGE:
  rg [OPTIONS] PATTERN [PATH ...]

POSITIONAL ARGUMENTS:
  <PATTERN>   A regular expression used for searching.
  <PATH>...   A file or directory to search.

INPUT OPTIONS:
  -e, --regexp=PATTERN            A pattern to search for.
  -f, --file=PATTERNFILE          Search for patterns from the given file.
  --pre=COMMAND                   Search output of COMMAND for each PATH.
  --pre-glob=GLOB                 Include or exclude files from a preprocessor.
  -z, --search-zip                Search in compressed files.

SEARCH OPTIONS:
  -s, --case-sensitive            Search case sensitively (default).
  --crlf                          Use CRLF line terminators (nice for Windows).
  --dfa-size-limit=NUM            The upper size limit of the regex DFA.
  -E, --encoding=ENCODING         Specify the text encoding of files to search.
  --engine=ENGINE                 Specify which regex engine to use.
  -F, --fixed-strings             Treat all patterns as literals.
  -i, --ignore-case               Case insensitive search.
  -v, --invert-match              Invert matching.
  -x, --line-regexp               Show matches surrounded by line boundaries.
  -m, --max-count=NUM             Limit the number of matching lines.
  --mmap                          Search with memory maps when possible.
  -U, --multiline                 Enable searching across multiple lines.
  --multiline-dotall              Make '.' match line terminators.
  --no-unicode                    Disable Unicode mode.
  --null-data                     Use NUL as a line terminator.
  -P, --pcre2                     Enable PCRE2 matching.
  --regex-size-limit=NUM          The size limit of the compiled regex.
  -S, --smart-case                Smart case search.
  --stop-on-nonmatch              Stop searching after a non-match.
  -a, --text                      Search binary files as if they were text.
  -j, --threads=NUM               Set the approximate number of threads to use.
  -w, --word-regexp               Show matches surrounded by word boundaries.
  --auto-hybrid-regex             (DEPRECATED) Use PCRE2 if appropriate.
  --no-pcre2-unicode              (DEPRECATED) Disable Unicode mode for PCRE2.

FILTER OPTIONS:
  --binary                        Search binary files.
  -L, --follow                    Follow symbolic links.
  -g, --glob=GLOB                 Include or exclude file paths.
  --glob-case-insensitive         Process all glob patterns case insensitively.
  -., --hidden                    Search hidden files and directories.
  --iglob=GLOB                    Include/exclude paths case insensitively.
  --ignore-file=PATH              Specify additional ignore files.
  --ignore-file-case-insensitive  Process ignore files case insensitively.
  -d, --max-depth=NUM             Descend at most NUM directories.
  --max-filesize=NUM              Ignore files larger than NUM in size.
  --no-ignore                     Don't use ignore files.
  --no-ignore-dot                 Don't use .ignore or .rgignore files.
  --no-ignore-exclude             Don't use local exclusion files.
  --no-ignore-files               Don't use --ignore-file arguments.
  --no-ignore-global              Don't use global ignore files.
  --no-ignore-parent              Don't use ignore files in parent directories.
  --no-ignore-vcs                 Don't use ignore files from source control.
  --no-require-git                Use .gitignore outside of git repositories.
  --one-file-system               Skip directories on other file systems.
  -t, --type=TYPE                 Only search files matching TYPE.
  -T, --type-not=TYPE             Do not search files matching TYPE.
  --type-add=TYPESPEC             Add a new glob for a file type.
  --type-clear=TYPE               Clear globs for a file type.
  -u, --unrestricted              Reduce the level of "smart" filtering.

OUTPUT OPTIONS:
  -A, --after-context=NUM         Show NUM lines after each match.
  -B, --before-context=NUM        Show NUM lines before each match.
  --block-buffered                Force block buffering.
  -b, --byte-offset               Print the byte offset for each matching line.
  --color=WHEN                    When to use color.
  --colors=COLOR_SPEC             Configure color settings and styles.
  --column                        Show column numbers.
  -C, --context=NUM               Show NUM lines before and after each match.
  --context-separator=SEP         Set the separator for contextual chunks.
  --field-context-separator=SEP   Set the field context separator.
  --field-match-separator=SEP     Set the field match separator.
  --heading                       Print matches grouped by each file.
  -h, --help                      Show help output.
  --hostname-bin=COMMAND          Run a program to get this system's hostname.
  --hyperlink-format=FORMAT       Set the format of hyperlinks.
  --include-zero                  Include zero matches in summary output.
  --line-buffered                 Force line buffering.
  -n, --line-number               Show line numbers.
  -N, --no-line-number            Suppress line numbers.
  -M, --max-columns=NUM           Omit lines longer than this limit.
  --max-columns-preview           Show preview for lines exceeding the limit.
  -0, --null                      Print a NUL byte after file paths.
  -o, --only-matching             Print only matched parts of a line.
  --path-separator=SEP            Set the path separator for printing paths.
  --passthru                      Print both matching and non-matching lines.
  -p, --pretty                    Alias for colors, headings and line numbers.
  -q, --quiet                     Do not print anything to stdout.
  -r, --replace=TEXT              Replace matches with the given text.
  --sort=SORTBY                   Sort results in ascending order.
  --sortr=SORTBY                  Sort results in descending order.
  --trim                          Trim prefix whitespace from matches.
  --vimgrep                       Print results in a vim compatible format.
  -H, --with-filename             Print the file path with each matching line.
  -I, --no-filename               Never print the path with each matching line.
  --sort-files                    (DEPRECATED) Sort results by file path.

OUTPUT MODES:
  -c, --count                     Show count of matching lines for each file.
  --count-matches                 Show count of every match for each file.
  -l, --files-with-matches        Print the paths with at least one match.
  --files-without-match           Print the paths that contain zero matches.
  --json                          Show search results in a JSON Lines format.

LOGGING OPTIONS:
  --debug                         Show debug messages.
  --no-ignore-messages            Suppress gitignore parse error messages.
  --no-messages                   Suppress some error messages.
  --stats                         Print statistics about the search.
  --trace                         Show trace messages.

OTHER BEHAVIORS:
  --files                         Print each file that would be searched.
  --generate=KIND                 Generate man pages and completion scripts.
  --no-config                     Never read configuration files.
  --pcre2-version                 Print the version of PCRE2 that ripgrep uses.
  --type-list                     Show all supported file types.
  -V, --version                   Print ripgrep's version.

def eprint(msg: str, opts: Optional[Options] = None):
    if opts is not None and opts.no_messages:
        return
    print(msg, file=sys.stderr)

def is_stdin_pipe() -> bool:
    try:
        mode = os.fstat(0).st_mode
    except OSError:
        return False
    return stat.S_ISFIFO(mode) or stat.S_ISREG(mode)

def apply_config(argv: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    if "--no-config" in argv:
        return argv
    cfg = os.environ.get("RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH")
    if not cfg:
        return argv
    try:
        tokens: list[str] = []
        with open(cfg, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.strip()
                if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                    continue
                tokens.append(line)
        return tokens + argv
    except OSError:
        return argv

def need_value(args: list[str], i: int, flag: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
    if i + 1 >= len(args):
        raise RGError(f"rg: flag {flag} requires a value")
    return args[i+1], i+2

def parse_num(s: str, flag: str) -> int:
    try:
        if s.startswith("-"):
            raise ValueError
        return int(s)
    except ValueError:
        raise RGError(f"rg: invalid value for {flag}: {s}")

def parse_size(s: str) -> int:
    m = re.fullmatch(r"([0-9]+)([KMGkmg]?)", s)
    if not m:
        raise RGError(f"rg: invalid size: {s}")
    n = int(m.group(1)); suf = m.group(2).lower()
    return n * ({"":1, "k":1024, "m":1024**2, "g":1024**3}[suf])

def add_type_spec(spec: str):
    # ripgrep syntax: name:glob,name:include:glob. Accept the common forms.
    if ":" not in spec:
        return
    parts = spec.split(":")
    if len(parts) >= 2:
        name = parts[0]
        glob = parts[-1]
        TYPE_GLOBS.setdefault(name, []).append(glob)

def parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> tuple[Options, bool]:
    argv = apply_config(argv)
    opts = Options()
    positionals: list[str] = []
    patterns_from_flags = False
    i = 0
    endopts = False
    noops_with_val = {
        "--dfa-size-limit", "--regex-size-limit", "--engine", "--hostname-bin",
        "--hyperlink-format", "--colors", "--ignore-file", "--type-clear",
        "--generate", "--line-terminator", "--pre", "--pre-glob",
    }
    noops_bool = {
        "--mmap", "--no-mmap", "--no-unicode", "--crlf", "--no-crlf",
        "--auto-hybrid-regex", "--no-pcre2-unicode", "--block-buffered",
        "--line-buffered", "--no-ignore-dot", "--no-ignore-exclude",
        "--no-ignore-files", "--no-ignore-global", "--no-ignore-parent",
        "--no-ignore-vcs", "--one-file-system", "--glob-case-insensitive",
        "--ignore-file-case-insensitive", "--no-ignore-messages", "--mmap",
        "--no-config", "--no-search-zip",
    }
    while i < len(argv):
        a = argv[i]
        if endopts or a == "-" or not a.startswith("-"):
            positionals.append(a); i += 1; continue
        if a == "--":
            endopts = True; i += 1; continue
        if a in ("-h", "--help"):
            print(SHORT_HELP if a == "-h" else LONG_HELP, end="")
            return opts, True
        if a in ("-V", "--version"):
            print(VERSION)
            print("")
            print("features:-pcre2")
            print("simd(compile):+SSE2,-SSSE3,-AVX2")
            print("simd(runtime):+SSE2,+SSSE3,+AVX2")
            print("")
            print("PCRE2 is not available in this build of ripgrep.")
            return opts, True
        if a == "--pcre2-version":
            print("PCRE2 is not available in this build of ripgrep.")
            sys.exit(1)
        if a in ("-P", "--pcre2"):
            eprint("rg: PCRE2 is not available in this build of ripgrep")
            sys.exit(2)
        if a == "--type-list":
            for name in sorted(TYPE_GLOBS):
                print(f"{name}: {', '.join(TYPE_GLOBS[name])}")
            return opts, True
        if a == "--files": opts.files = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--debug": opts.debug = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--trace": opts.trace = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--stats": opts.stats = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--json": opts.json = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--binary": opts.binary = True; i += 1; continue
        if a in ("--text",): opts.text = True; i += 1; continue
        if a in ("--hidden",): opts.hidden = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--no-ignore": opts.no_ignore = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--no-require-git": opts.no_require_git = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--fixed-strings": opts.fixed = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--ignore-case": opts.ignore_case = True; opts.case_sensitive_set = False; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--case-sensitive": opts.ignore_case = False; opts.smart_case = False; opts.case_sensitive_set = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--smart-case": opts.smart_case = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--invert-match": opts.invert = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--line-regexp": opts.line_regexp = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--word-regexp": opts.word_regexp = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--line-number": opts.line_number = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--no-line-number": opts.line_number = False; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--with-filename": opts.with_filename = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--no-filename": opts.with_filename = False; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--column": opts.column = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--byte-offset": opts.byte_offset = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--only-matching": opts.only_matching = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--count": opts.count = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--count-matches": opts.count_matches = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--files-with-matches": opts.files_with_matches = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--files-without-match": opts.files_without_match = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--quiet": opts.quiet = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--heading": opts.heading = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--no-heading": opts.heading = False; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--vimgrep": opts.vimgrep = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--passthru": opts.passthru = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--trim": opts.trim = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--include-zero": opts.include_zero = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--no-messages": opts.no_messages = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--null": opts.null = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--search-zip": opts.search_zip = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--multiline": opts.multiline = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--multiline-dotall": opts.multiline_dotall = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == "--pretty":
            opts.color = "always"; opts.heading = True; opts.line_number = True; i += 1; continue
        # Long options with --name=value or --name value
        if a.startswith("--"):
            name, eq, val = a.partition("=")
            def getval() -> str:
                nonlocal i, val, eq
                if eq:
                    i += 1; return val
                v, ni = need_value(argv, i, name); i = ni; return v
            if name == "--regexp": opts.patterns.append(getval()); patterns_from_flags = True; continue
            if name == "--file": opts.pattern_files.append(getval()); patterns_from_flags = True; continue
            if name == "--glob": opts.globs.append((getval(), not getval if False else True, False)); continue
            if name == "--iglob": opts.globs.append((getval(), True, True)); continue
            if name == "--type": opts.type_include.append(getval()); continue
            if name == "--type-not": opts.type_exclude.append(getval()); continue
            if name == "--type-add": add_type_spec(getval()); continue
            if name == "--after-context": opts.after = parse_num(getval(), name); continue
            if name == "--before-context": opts.before = parse_num(getval(), name); continue
            if name == "--context": n = parse_num(getval(), name); opts.after = n; opts.before = n; continue
            if name == "--max-count": opts.max_count = parse_num(getval(), name); continue
            if name == "--max-depth": opts.max_depth = parse_num(getval(), name); continue
            if name == "--max-filesize": opts.max_filesize = parse_size(getval()); continue
            if name == "--max-columns": opts.max_columns = parse_num(getval(), name); continue
            if name == "--replace": opts.replace = getval(); continue
            if name == "--color": opts.color = getval(); continue
            if name == "--sort": opts.sort = getval(); continue
            if name == "--sortr": opts.sortr = getval(); continue
            if name == "--path-separator": opts.path_separator = getval(); continue
            if name == "--context-separator": opts.context_separator = getval(); continue
            if name == "--field-match-separator": opts.field_match_separator = getval(); continue
            if name == "--field-context-separator": opts.field_context_separator = getval(); continue
            if name == "--encoding": opts.encoding = getval(); continue
            if name == "--pre": opts.pre = getval(); continue
            if name == "--pre-glob": opts.pre_globs.append(getval()); continue
            if name in noops_with_val:
                _ = getval(); continue
            if name in noops_bool:
                i += 1; continue
            raise RGError(f"rg: unrecognized flag {a}")
        # short options, maybe combined
        if a.startswith("-") and len(a) > 1:
            j = 1
            while j < len(a):
                ch = a[j]
                rest = a[j+1:]
                def short_val(flag: str) -> str:
                    nonlocal i, j
                    if rest:
                        j = len(a)
                        return rest
                    v, ni = need_value(argv, i, flag)
                    i = ni - 1
                    j = len(a)
                    return v
                if ch == "e": opts.patterns.append(short_val("-e")); patterns_from_flags = True
                elif ch == "f": opts.pattern_files.append(short_val("-f")); patterns_from_flags = True
                elif ch == "g":
                    pat = short_val("-g"); opts.globs.append((pat, True, False))
                elif ch == "t": opts.type_include.append(short_val("-t"))
                elif ch == "T": opts.type_exclude.append(short_val("-T"))
                elif ch == "A": opts.after = parse_num(short_val("-A"), "-A")
                elif ch == "B": opts.before = parse_num(short_val("-B"), "-B")
                elif ch == "C": n = parse_num(short_val("-C"), "-C"); opts.after = n; opts.before = n
                elif ch == "m": opts.max_count = parse_num(short_val("-m"), "-m")
                elif ch == "d": opts.max_depth = parse_num(short_val("-d"), "-d")
                elif ch == "M": opts.max_columns = parse_num(short_val("-M"), "-M")
                elif ch == "r": opts.replace = short_val("-r")
                elif ch == "E": opts.encoding = short_val("-E")
                elif ch == "j": _ = short_val("-j")
                elif ch == "s": opts.ignore_case = False; opts.smart_case = False; opts.case_sensitive_set = True
                elif ch == "i": opts.ignore_case = True; opts.case_sensitive_set = False
                elif ch == "S": opts.smart_case = True
                elif ch == "F": opts.fixed = True
                elif ch == "v": opts.invert = True
                elif ch == "x": opts.line_regexp = True
                elif ch == "w": opts.word_regexp = True
                elif ch == "a": opts.text = True
                elif ch == "L": opts.follow = True
                elif ch == ".": opts.hidden = True
                elif ch == "u": opts.unrestricted += 1
                elif ch == "n": opts.line_number = True
                elif ch == "N": opts.line_number = False
                elif ch == "H": opts.with_filename = True
                elif ch == "I": opts.with_filename = False
                elif ch == "b": opts.byte_offset = True
                elif ch == "o": opts.only_matching = True
                elif ch == "c": opts.count = True
                elif ch == "l": opts.files_with_matches = True
                elif ch == "q": opts.quiet = True
                elif ch == "p": opts.color = "always"; opts.heading = True; opts.line_number = True
                elif ch == "0": opts.null = True
                elif ch == "z": opts.search_zip = True
                elif ch == "U": opts.multiline = True
                else:
                    raise RGError(f"rg: unrecognized flag -{ch}")
                j += 1
            i += 1; continue
    if opts.unrestricted >= 1:
        opts.no_ignore = True
    if opts.unrestricted >= 2:
        opts.hidden = True
    if opts.unrestricted >= 3:
        opts.text = True
    # Correct globs with ! exclusion.
    fixed_globs = []
    for pat, inc, ci in opts.globs:
        if pat.startswith("!"):
            fixed_globs.append((pat[1:], False, ci))
        else:
            fixed_globs.append((pat, True, ci))
    opts.globs = fixed_globs
    for pf in opts.pattern_files:
        try:
            with open(pf, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
                for line in f:
                    opts.patterns.append(line.rstrip("\n"))
        except OSError as e:
            raise RGError(f"rg: {pf}: {e.strerror} (os error {getattr(e, 'errno', 0)})")
    if opts.files:
        opts.paths = positionals[:] or ["."]
    else:
        if not patterns_from_flags:
            if not positionals:
                raise RGError("rg: ripgrep requires at least one pattern to execute a search")
            opts.patterns.append(positionals[0])
            opts.paths = positionals[1:]
        else:
            opts.paths = positionals[:]
        if not opts.paths:
            opts.paths = ["-"] if is_stdin_pipe() else ["."]
    return opts, False

# ---------- pattern compilation ----------

def contains_upper(patterns: list[str]) -> bool:
    return any(any(c.isalpha() and c.upper() == c and c.lower() != c for c in p) for p in patterns)

def translate_regex(p: str) -> str:
    # A small compatibility layer for a few Rust-regex conveniences commonly used.
    repls = {
        r"\p{L}": r"[^\W\d_]",
        r"\pL": r"[^\W\d_]",
        r"\p{Letter}": r"[^\W\d_]",
        r"\p{Alphabetic}": r"[^\W\d_]",
        r"\p{N}": r"\d",
        r"\pN": r"\d",
        r"\p{Number}": r"\d",
        r"\p{Greek}": r"[\u0370-\u03ff]",
    }
    for k, v in repls.items():
        p = p.replace(k, v)
    return p

def compile_pattern(opts: Options):
    pats = opts.patterns[:] or [""]
    if opts.fixed:
        pats = [re.escape(p) for p in pats]
    else:
        pats = [translate_regex(p) for p in pats]
    body = "|".join(f"(?:{p})" for p in pats)
    if opts.line_regexp:
        body = f"^(?:{body})$"
    if opts.word_regexp:
        body = f"\\b(?:{body})\\b"
    flags = re.MULTILINE
    if opts.multiline_dotall:
        flags |= re.DOTALL
    if opts.ignore_case or (opts.smart_case and not contains_upper(opts.patterns)):
        flags |= re.IGNORECASE
    try:
        return re.compile(body, flags)
    except re.error as e:
        # Approximate ripgrep's diagnostic.
        pat = opts.patterns[0] if opts.patterns else body
        eprint("rg: regex parse error:")
        eprint(f"    (?:{pat})")
        eprint("       ^")
        eprint(f"error: {str(e)}")
        sys.exit(2)

# ---------- file discovery and filters ----------

def path_has_git(start: str) -> bool:
    d = os.path.abspath(start if os.path.isdir(start) else os.path.dirname(start) or ".")
    while True:
        if os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, ".git")):
            return True
        nd = os.path.dirname(d)
        if nd == d:
            return False
        d = nd

def load_ignore_file(path: str) -> list[str]:
    pats: list[str] = []
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.rstrip("\n")
                if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                    continue
                if line.startswith("\\#"):
                    line = line[1:]
                pats.append(line)
    except OSError:
        pass
    return pats

def ignore_patterns_for_root(root: str, opts: Options) -> list[str]:
    if opts.no_ignore:
        return []
    pats: list[str] = []
    base = root if os.path.isdir(root) else os.path.dirname(root) or "."
    use_gitignore = opts.no_require_git or path_has_git(base)
    if use_gitignore:
        pats += load_ignore_file(os.path.join(base, ".gitignore"))
    pats += load_ignore_file(os.path.join(base, ".ignore"))
    pats += load_ignore_file(os.path.join(base, ".rgignore"))
    return pats

def match_gitignore(rel: str, is_dir: bool, patterns: list[str]) -> bool:
    ignored = False
    rel = rel.replace(os.sep, "/")
    name = rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    for raw in patterns:
        neg = raw.startswith("!")
        pat = raw[1:] if neg else raw
        dir_only = pat.endswith("/")
        if dir_only:
            pat = pat.rstrip("/")
        if dir_only and not is_dir and not (rel == pat or rel.startswith(pat + "/")):
            continue
        anchored = "/" in pat
        ok = False
        if dir_only:
            ok = rel == pat or rel.startswith(pat + "/")
        elif anchored:
            ok = fnmatch.fnmatch(rel, pat)
        else:
            ok = fnmatch.fnmatch(name, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(rel, pat)
        if ok:
            ignored = not neg
    return ignored

def is_hidden_path(rel: str) -> bool:
    parts = [p for p in rel.replace(os.sep, "/").split("/") if p and p != "."]
    return any(p.startswith(".") for p in parts)

def type_matches(path: str, typename: str) -> bool:
    globs = TYPE_GLOBS.get(typename, [])
    name = os.path.basename(path)
    norm = path.replace(os.sep, "/")
    return any(fnmatch.fnmatch(name, g) or fnmatch.fnmatch(norm, g) for g in globs)

def passes_globs(display: str, rel: str, opts: Options) -> bool:
    if not opts.globs:
        return True
    included_seen = any(inc for _, inc, _ in opts.globs)
    included = not included_seen
    for pat, inc, ci in opts.globs:
        target = rel.replace(os.sep, "/")
        target2 = display.replace(os.sep, "/")
        p = pat
        if ci:
            target = target.lower(); target2 = target2.lower(); p = p.lower()
        # Gitignore-style: glob without slash can match basename too.
        name = target.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
        ok = fnmatch.fnmatch(target, p) or fnmatch.fnmatch(target2, p) or fnmatch.fnmatch(name, p)
        if ok:
            included = inc
    return included

def passes_type(path: str, opts: Options) -> bool:
    if opts.type_include and not any(type_matches(path, t) for t in opts.type_include):
        return False
    if opts.type_exclude and any(type_matches(path, t) for t in opts.type_exclude):
        return False
    return True

def display_for(root: str, rel: str, explicit_root: str, is_default: bool) -> str:
    relp = rel.replace(os.sep, "/")
    if relp == ".":
        relp = os.path.basename(root)
    if os.path.isfile(root):
        return explicit_root
    if explicit_root in (".", "./") or explicit_root.startswith("./"):
        return "./" + relp if relp else "./"
    if is_default:
        return relp
    prefix = explicit_root.rstrip("/")
    return (prefix + "/" + relp) if relp else explicit_root

def iter_files_for_root(root_arg: str, opts: Options, is_default: bool=False) -> Iterator[tuple[str, str]]:
    if root_arg == "-":
        yield "-", "-"; return
    root = root_arg
    if not os.path.exists(root):
        raise FileNotFoundError(root)
    ignore_pats = ignore_patterns_for_root(root, opts)
    if os.path.isfile(root):
        disp = root_arg
        rel = os.path.basename(root)
        if opts.max_filesize is not None:
            try:
                if os.path.getsize(root) > opts.max_filesize:
                    return
            except OSError:
                pass
        if passes_globs(disp, rel, opts) and passes_type(root, opts):
            yield root, disp
        return
    base = root
    # stack-based traversal; reverse scandir entries gives output close to rg's walk in many cases.
    stack: list[tuple[str, int]] = [(base, 0)]
    while stack:
        d, depth = stack.pop()
        try:
            entries = list(os.scandir(d))
        except OSError as e:
            eprint(f"rg: {d}: IO error for operation on {d}: {e.strerror} (os error {e.errno})", opts)
            continue
        dirs = []
        files = []
        for ent in entries:
            rel = os.path.relpath(ent.path, base)
            if rel == ".": rel = ent.name
            rel_slash = rel.replace(os.sep, "/")
            try:
                isdir = ent.is_dir(follow_symlinks=opts.follow)
                isfile = ent.is_file(follow_symlinks=opts.follow)
            except OSError:
                continue
            # Hidden directories and files.
            if not opts.hidden and is_hidden_path(rel_slash):
                continue
            if match_gitignore(rel_slash, isdir, ignore_pats):
                continue
            if isdir:
                if opts.max_depth is None or depth + 1 < opts.max_depth:
                    dirs.append(ent.path)
            elif isfile:
                disp = display_for(base, rel, root_arg, is_default)
                if opts.max_filesize is not None:
                    try:
                        if ent.stat(follow_symlinks=opts.follow).st_size > opts.max_filesize:
                            continue
                    except OSError:
                        continue
                if passes_globs(disp, rel_slash, opts) and passes_type(ent.path, opts):
                    files.append((ent.path, disp))
        # Files before descending, with reverse-ish natural order like ripgrep's parallel walker often shows.
        for f in reversed(files):
            yield f
        for dd in dirs:
            stack.append((dd, depth + 1))

def gather_files(opts: Options) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    roots = opts.paths or ["."]
    out: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    default = (roots == ["."] and not opts.files)
    for r in roots:
        try:
            out.extend(list(iter_files_for_root(r, opts, is_default=default)))
        except FileNotFoundError:
            eprint(f"rg: {r}: IO error for operation on {r}: No such file or directory (os error 2)", opts)
            raise
    sortkey = opts.sort or ("path" if False else None)
    reverse = False
    if opts.sortr:
        sortkey = opts.sortr; reverse = True
    if sortkey or opts.sort == "path":
        if sortkey in ("path", "none", None):
            out.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=reverse)
        elif sortkey in ("modified", "accessed", "created"):
            idx = {"modified":"st_mtime", "accessed":"st_atime", "created":"st_ctime"}[sortkey]
            out.sort(key=lambda x: getattr(os.stat(x[0]), idx, 0), reverse=reverse)
        else:
            out.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=reverse)
    return out

# ---------- reading/searching/printing ----------

def decode_bytes(data: bytes, opts: Options) -> str:
    enc = opts.encoding.lower()
    if enc in ("none", "auto", ""):
        if data.startswith(b"\xff\xfe") or data.startswith(b"\xfe\xff"):
            try:
                return data.decode("utf-16")
            except UnicodeDecodeError:
                pass
        if data.startswith(b"\xef\xbb\xbf"):
            try:
                return data.decode("utf-8-sig", errors="replace")
            except Exception:
                pass
        return data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    aliases = {"latin-1":"latin1", "utf-16le":"utf-16le", "utf-16be":"utf-16be"}
    try:
        return data.decode(aliases.get(enc, enc), errors="replace")
    except LookupError:
        return data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

def read_file(path: str, opts: Options) -> bytes:
    if path == "-":
        return sys.stdin.buffer.read()
    if opts.pre:
        try:
            cp = subprocess.run([opts.pre, path], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
            return cp.stdout
        except Exception:
            pass
    if opts.search_zip:
        low = path.lower()
        try:
            if low.endswith((".gz", ".tgz")):
                with gzip.open(path, "rb") as f: return f.read()
            if low.endswith(".bz2"):
                with bz2.open(path, "rb") as f: return f.read()
            if low.endswith((".xz", ".lzma")):
                with lzma.open(path, "rb") as f: return f.read()
        except Exception:
            pass
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        return f.read()

def split_lines_keep(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
    # Return (line_without_final_newline, byte-ish char offset). Keep embedded NULs.
    lines: list[tuple[str, int]] = []
    off = 0
    for part in text.splitlines(True):
        raw = part
        line = raw[:-1] if raw.endswith("\n") else raw
        if line.endswith("\r"):
            line = line[:-1]
        lines.append((line, off))
        off += len(raw.encode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
    if text == "":
        return []
    if not text.endswith(("\n", "\r")):
        # splitlines(True) already included last line.
        pass
    return lines

def format_replacement(template: str, m: re.Match) -> str:
    out = ""
    i = 0
    while i < len(template):
        c = template[i]
        if c == "$" and i + 1 < len(template):
            j = i + 1
            if template[j] == "$":
                out += "$"; i += 2; continue
            if template[j] == "0":
                out += m.group(0); i += 2; continue
            if template[j].isdigit():
                k = j
                while k < len(template) and template[k].isdigit(): k += 1
                try:
                    out += m.group(int(template[j:k])) or ""
                except Exception:
                    pass
                i = k; continue
            if template[j] == "{":
                k = template.find("}", j+1)
                if k != -1:
                    name = template[j+1:k]
                    try:
                        out += m.group(name) or ""
                    except Exception:
                        pass
                    i = k+1; continue
        out += c; i += 1
    return out

def replace_line(line: str, regex, opts: Options) -> str:
    if opts.replace is None:
        return line
    return regex.sub(lambda m: format_replacement(opts.replace or "", m), line)

def colorize_line(line: str, regex, opts: Options) -> str:
    use = opts.color == "always" or (opts.color == "auto" and sys.stdout.isatty())
    if not use or opts.invert:
        return line
    return regex.sub(lambda m: "\x1b[0m\x1b[1m\x1b[31m" + m.group(0) + "\x1b[0m", line)

def c_path(path: str, opts: Options) -> str:
    if opts.path_separator and opts.path_separator != "/":
        path = path.replace("/", opts.path_separator)
    if opts.color == "always":
        return "\x1b[0m\x1b[35m" + path + "\x1b[0m"
    return path

def c_num(n: int | str, opts: Options) -> str:
    if opts.color == "always":
        return "\x1b[0m\x1b[32m" + str(n) + "\x1b[0m"
    return str(n)

def should_with_filename(opts: Options, nfiles: int, path: str) -> bool:
    if opts.with_filename is not None:
        return opts.with_filename
    return path != "-" and nfiles > 1

def should_line_number(opts: Options) -> bool:
    return bool(opts.line_number)

def print_out(s: str, stats: Stats):
    if not s.endswith("\n"):
        s += "\n"
    stats.bytes_printed += len(s.encode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
    sys.stdout.write(s)

def prefix_fields(path: str, lineno: int, col: Optional[int], byteoff: Optional[int], opts: Options, nfiles: int, context: bool=False) -> str:
    sep = opts.field_context_separator if context else opts.field_match_separator
    fields: list[str] = []
    if should_with_filename(opts, nfiles, path):
        fields.append(c_path(path, opts))
    if should_line_number(opts) or opts.vimgrep:
        fields.append(c_num(lineno, opts))
    if opts.column or opts.vimgrep:
        fields.append(c_num(col if col is not None else 1, opts))
    if opts.byte_offset:
        fields.append(c_num(byteoff if byteoff is not None else 0, opts))
    if not fields:
        return ""
    return sep.join(str(f) for f in fields) + sep

def line_matches(line: str, regex, opts: Options) -> tuple[bool, list[re.Match]]:
    ms = list(regex.finditer(line))
    matched = bool(ms)
    if opts.invert:
        return (not matched), []
    return matched, ms

def binary_message(path: str, nfiles: int, nuloff: int, opts: Options, stats: Stats):
    prefix = ""
    if should_with_filename(opts, nfiles, path):
        prefix = c_path(path, opts) + opts.field_match_separator + " "
    print_out(f'{prefix}binary file matches (found "\\0" byte around offset {nuloff})', stats)

def json_line(obj: dict, stats: Stats):
    s = json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
    print_out(s, stats)

def search_one(path: str, disp: str, data: bytes, regex, opts: Options, stats: Stats, nfiles: int) -> bool:
    stats.searches += 1
    stats.bytes_searched += len(data)
    nuloff = data.find(b"\0")
    text = decode_bytes(data, opts)
    lines = split_lines_keep(text)
    has_binary = nuloff >= 0 and not opts.text
    # Find matches first for modes that need whole-file counts/context.
    records = []  # dicts: line, lineno, off, matches, matched
    matched_lines_count = 0
    total_matches = 0
    for idx, (line, off) in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        matched, ms = line_matches(line, regex, opts)
        if opts.passthru and not matched:
            pass
        if matched:
            matched_lines_count += 1
            total_matches += max(1 if opts.invert else 0, len(ms))
            records.append({"idx": idx-1, "lineno": idx, "line": line, "off": off, "matches": ms, "matched": True})
            if opts.max_count is not None and matched_lines_count >= opts.max_count:
                # ripgrep stops after this many matching lines per file.
                break
    file_has_match = matched_lines_count > 0
    if file_has_match:
        stats.searches_with_match += 1
        stats.any_match = True
        stats.matched_lines += matched_lines_count
        stats.matches += total_matches
    if opts.quiet:
        return file_has_match
    if opts.json:
        json_line({"type":"begin","data":{"path":{"text":disp}}}, stats)
        for r in records:
            line = r["line"]
            full_line = line + "\n"
            subs = []
            for m in r["matches"]:
                subs.append({"match":{"text":m.group(0)},"start":m.start(),"end":m.end()})
            json_line({"type":"match","data":{"path":{"text":disp},"lines":{"text":full_line},"line_number":r["lineno"],"absolute_offset":r["off"],"submatches":subs}}, stats)
        json_line({"type":"end","data":{"path":{"text":disp},"binary_offset":None,"stats":{"elapsed":{"secs":0,"nanos":0,"human":"0.000000s"},"searches":1,"searches_with_match":1 if file_has_match else 0,"bytes_searched":len(data),"bytes_printed":0,"matched_lines":matched_lines_count,"matches":total_matches}}}, stats)
        return file_has_match
    if opts.count or opts.count_matches:
        val = total_matches if opts.count_matches else matched_lines_count
        if file_has_match or opts.include_zero or nfiles > 1:
            prefix = ""
            if should_with_filename(opts, nfiles, disp):
                prefix = c_path(disp, opts) + opts.field_match_separator
            print_out(f"{prefix}{val}", stats)
        return file_has_match
    if opts.files_with_matches:
        if file_has_match:
            sys.stdout.write(disp + ("\0" if opts.null else "\n")); stats.bytes_printed += len(disp)+1
        return file_has_match
    if opts.files_without_match:
        if not file_has_match:
            sys.stdout.write(disp + ("\0" if opts.null else "\n")); stats.bytes_printed += len(disp)+1
        return file_has_match
    if has_binary and file_has_match:
        binary_message(disp, nfiles, nuloff, opts, stats)
        return True
    if not file_has_match and not opts.passthru:
        return False
    # Context output: build set of line indices to print.
    matched_indices = {r["idx"] for r in records}
    to_print: dict[int, bool] = {}
    if opts.passthru:
        for i in range(len(lines)):
            to_print[i] = i in matched_indices
    else:
        for mi in matched_indices:
            for j in range(max(0, mi - opts.before), min(len(lines), mi + opts.after + 1)):
                to_print[j] = j in matched_indices
    # Heading groups.
    if opts.heading and should_with_filename(opts, nfiles, disp):
        print_out(c_path(disp, opts), stats)
    printed_any = False
    last_i: Optional[int] = None
    for i in sorted(to_print):
        if last_i is not None and i > last_i + 1 and (opts.before or opts.after) and not opts.heading:
            print_out(opts.context_separator, stats)
        line, off = lines[i]
        ismatch = to_print[i]
        lineno = i + 1
        matched, ms = line_matches(line, regex, opts)
        if opts.max_columns is not None and len(line) > opts.max_columns and not opts.max_columns_preview:
            line_to_show = f"[Omitted long line with {len(line)} columns]"
        else:
            line_to_show = line.lstrip() if opts.trim else line
        if opts.only_matching and ismatch and not opts.invert:
            for m in ms:
                txt = format_replacement(opts.replace, m) if opts.replace is not None else m.group(0)
                col = m.start() + 1
                boff = off + len(line[:m.start()].encode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
                pref = prefix_fields(disp, lineno, col, boff, opts, nfiles, context=False)
                print_out(pref + colorize_line(txt, regex, opts), stats)
        elif opts.vimgrep and ismatch and not opts.invert:
            for m in ms or [None]:
                col = (m.start() + 1) if m else 1
                boff = off + (len(line[:m.start()].encode("utf-8", errors="replace")) if m else 0)
                pref = prefix_fields(disp, lineno, col, boff, opts, nfiles, context=False)
                print_out(pref + colorize_line(replace_line(line_to_show, regex, opts), regex, opts), stats)
        else:
            first_col = (ms[0].start() + 1) if ms else 1
            pref = "" if opts.heading and should_with_filename(opts, nfiles, disp) else prefix_fields(disp, lineno, first_col, off, opts, nfiles, context=not ismatch)
            out_line = replace_line(line_to_show, regex, opts) if ismatch else line_to_show
            out_line = colorize_line(out_line, regex, opts) if ismatch else out_line
            print_out(pref + out_line, stats)
        printed_any = True
        last_i = i
    if opts.heading and printed_any:
        # Blank line between file groups; main loop suppresses final exactness not vital.
        pass
    return file_has_match

def print_files(opts: Options) -> int:
    stats = Stats()
    had_error = False
    try:
        files = gather_files(opts)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return 2
    if opts.sort == "path" or opts.sort is None and False:
        pass
    for _, disp in files:
        sys.stdout.write(disp + ("\0" if opts.null else "\n"))
        stats.bytes_printed += len(disp)+1
    return 0 if files else 1

def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    try:
        opts, done = parse_args(argv)
    except RGError as e:
        eprint(str(e))
        return 2
    if done:
        return 0
    if opts.files:
        return print_files(opts)
    regex = compile_pattern(opts)
    stats = Stats()
    try:
        files = gather_files(opts)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return 2
    nfiles = len(files)
    had_error = False
    heading_need_blank = False
    for idx, (path, disp) in enumerate(files):
        try:
            data = read_file(path, opts)
        except OSError as e:
            stats.errors += 1; had_error = True
            eprint(f"rg: {disp}: IO error for operation on {disp}: {e.strerror} (os error {e.errno})", opts)
            continue
        before_bytes = stats.bytes_printed

            if name in noops_bool:

            raise RGError(f"rg: unrecognized flag {a}")
        # short options, maybe combined
        if a.startswith("-") and len(a) > 1:
            j = 1
            while j < len(a):
                ch = a[j]
                rest = a[j+1:]
                def short_val(flag: str) -> str:
                    nonlocal i, j
                    if rest:
                        j = len(a)
                        return rest
                    v, ni = need_value(argv, i, flag)
                    i = ni - 1
                    j = len(a)
                    return v
                if ch == "e": opts.patterns.append(short_val("-e")); patterns_from_flags = True
                elif ch == "f": opts.pattern_files.append(short_val("-f")); patterns_from_flags = True
                elif ch == "g":
                    pat = short_val("-g"); opts.globs.append((pat, True, False))
                elif ch == "t": opts.type_include.append(short_val("-t"))
                elif ch == "T": opts.type_exclude.append(short_val("-T"))
                elif ch == "A": opts.after = parse_num(short_val("-A"), "-A")
                elif ch == "B": opts.before = parse_num(short_val("-B"), "-B")
                elif ch == "C": n = parse_num(short_val("-C"), "-C"); opts.after = n; opts.before = n
                elif ch == "m": opts.max_count = parse_num(short_val("-m"), "-m")
                elif ch == "d": opts.max_depth = parse_num(short_val("-d"), "-d")
                elif ch == "M": opts.max_columns = parse_num(short_val("-M"), "-M")
                elif ch == "r": opts.replace = short_val("-r")
                elif ch == "E": opts.encoding = short_val("-E")
                elif ch == "j": _ = short_val("-j")
                elif ch == "s": opts.ignore_case = False; opts.smart_case = False; opts.case_sensitive_set = True
                elif ch == "i": opts.ignore_case = True; opts.case_sensitive_set = False
                elif ch == "S": opts.smart_case = True
                elif ch == "F": opts.fixed = True
                elif ch == "v": opts.invert = True
                elif ch == "x": opts.line_regexp = True
                elif ch == "w": opts.word_regexp = True
                elif ch == "a": opts.text = True
                elif ch == "L": opts.follow = True
                elif ch == ".": opts.hidden = True
                elif ch == "u": opts.unrestricted += 1
                elif ch == "n": opts.line_number = True
                elif ch == "N": opts.line_number = False
                elif ch == "H": opts.with_filename = True
                elif ch == "I": opts.with_filename = False
                elif ch == "b": opts.byte_offset = True
                elif ch == "o": opts.only_matching = True
                elif ch == "c": opts.count = True
                elif ch == "l": opts.files_with_matches = True
                elif ch == "q": opts.quiet = True
                elif ch == "p": opts.color = "always"; opts.heading = True; opts.line_number = True
                elif ch == "0": opts.null = True
                elif ch == "z": opts.search_zip = True
                elif ch == "U": opts.multiline = True
                else:
                    raise RGError(f"rg: unrecognized flag -{ch}")
                j += 1
            i += 1; continue
    if opts.unrestricted >= 1:
        opts.no_ignore = True
    if opts.unrestricted >= 2:
        opts.hidden = True
    if opts.unrestricted >= 3:
        opts.text = True
    # Correct globs with ! exclusion.
    fixed_globs = []
    for pat, inc, ci in opts.globs:
        if pat.startswith("!"):
            fixed_globs.append((pat[1:], False, ci))
        else:
            fixed_globs.append((pat, True, ci))
    opts.globs = fixed_globs
    for pf in opts.pattern_files:
        try:
            with open(pf, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
                for line in f:
                    opts.patterns.append(line.rstrip("\n"))
        except OSError as e:
            raise RGError(f"rg: {pf}: {e.strerror} (os error {getattr(e, 'errno', 0)})")
    if opts.files:
        opts.paths = positionals[:] or ["."]
    else:
        if not patterns_from_flags:
            if not positionals:
                raise RGError("rg: ripgrep requires at least one pattern to execute a search")
            opts.patterns.append(positionals[0])
            opts.paths = positionals[1:]
        else:
            opts.paths = positionals[:]
        if not opts.paths:
            opts.paths = ["-"] if is_stdin_pipe() else ["."]
    return opts, False

# ---------- pattern compilation ----------

def contains_upper(patterns: list[str]) -> bool:
    return any(any(c.isalpha() and c.upper() == c and c.lower() != c for c in p) for p in patterns)

def translate_regex(p: str) -> str:
    # A small compatibility layer for a few Rust-regex conveniences commonly used.
    repls = {
        r"\p{L}": r"[^\W\d_]",
        r"\pL": r"[^\W\d_]",
        r"\p{Letter}": r"[^\W\d_]",
        r"\p{Alphabetic}": r"[^\W\d_]",
        r"\p{N}": r"\d",
        r"\pN": r"\d",
        r"\p{Number}": r"\d",
        r"\p{Greek}": r"[\u0370-\u03ff]",
    }
    for k, v in repls.items():
        p = p.replace(k, v)
    return p

def compile_pattern(opts: Options):
    pats = opts.patterns[:] or [""]
    if opts.fixed:
        pats = [re.escape(p) for p in pats]
    else:
        pats = [translate_regex(p) for p in pats]
    body = "|".join(f"(?:{p})" for p in pats)
    if opts.line_regexp:
        body = f"^(?:{body})$"
    if opts.word_regexp:
        body = f"\\b(?:{body})\\b"
    flags = re.MULTILINE
    if opts.multiline_dotall:
        flags |= re.DOTALL
    if opts.ignore_case or (opts.smart_case and not contains_upper(opts.patterns)):
        flags |= re.IGNORECASE
    try:
        return re.compile(body, flags)
    except re.error as e:
        # Approximate ripgrep's diagnostic.
        pat = opts.patterns[0] if opts.patterns else body
        eprint("rg: regex parse error:")
        eprint(f"    (?:{pat})")
        eprint("       ^")
        eprint(f"error: {str(e)}")
        sys.exit(2)

# ---------- file discovery and filters ----------

def path_has_git(start: str) -> bool:
    d = os.path.abspath(start if os.path.isdir(start) else os.path.dirname(start) or ".")
    while True:
        if os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, ".git")):
            return True
        nd = os.path.dirname(d)
        if nd == d:
            return False
        d = nd

def load_ignore_file(path: str) -> list[str]:
    pats: list[str] = []
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.rstrip("\n")
                if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                    continue
                if line.startswith("\\#"):
                    line = line[1:]
                pats.append(line)
    except OSError:
        pass
    return pats

def ignore_patterns_for_root(root: str, opts: Options) -> list[str]:
    if opts.no_ignore:
        return []
    pats: list[str] = []
    base = root if os.path.isdir(root) else os.path.dirname(root) or "."
    use_gitignore = opts.no_require_git or path_has_git(base)
    if use_gitignore:
        pats += load_ignore_file(os.path.join(base, ".gitignore"))
    pats += load_ignore_file(os.path.join(base, ".ignore"))
    pats += load_ignore_file(os.path.join(base, ".rgignore"))
    return pats

def match_gitignore(rel: str, is_dir: bool, patterns: list[str]) -> bool:
    ignored = False
    rel = rel.replace(os.sep, "/")
    name = rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    for raw in patterns:
        neg = raw.startswith("!")
        pat = raw[1:] if neg else raw
        dir_only = pat.endswith("/")
        if dir_only:
            pat = pat.rstrip("/")
        if dir_only and not is_dir and not (rel == pat or rel.startswith(pat + "/")):
            continue
        anchored = "/" in pat
        ok = False
        if dir_only:
            ok = rel == pat or rel.startswith(pat + "/")
        elif anchored:
            ok = fnmatch.fnmatch(rel, pat)
        else:
            ok = fnmatch.fnmatch(name, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(rel, pat)
        if ok:
            ignored = not neg
    return ignored

def is_hidden_path(rel: str) -> bool:
    parts = [p for p in rel.replace(os.sep, "/").split("/") if p and p != "."]
    return any(p.startswith(".") for p in parts)

def type_matches(path: str, typename: str) -> bool:
    globs = TYPE_GLOBS.get(typename, [])
    name = os.path.basename(path)
    norm = path.replace(os.sep, "/")
    return any(fnmatch.fnmatch(name, g) or fnmatch.fnmatch(norm, g) for g in globs)

def passes_globs(display: str, rel: str, opts: Options) -> bool:
    if not opts.globs:
        return True
    included_seen = any(inc for _, inc, _ in opts.globs)
    included = not included_seen
    for pat, inc, ci in opts.globs:
        target = rel.replace(os.sep, "/")
        target2 = display.replace(os.sep, "/")
        p = pat
        if ci:
            target = target.lower(); target2 = target2.lower(); p = p.lower()
        # Gitignore-style: glob without slash can match basename too.
        name = target.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
        ok = fnmatch.fnmatch(target, p) or fnmatch.fnmatch(target2, p) or fnmatch.fnmatch(name, p)
        if ok:
            included = inc
    return included

def passes_type(path: str, opts: Options) -> bool:
    if opts.type_include and not any(type_matches(path, t) for t in opts.type_include):
        return False
    if opts.type_exclude and any(type_matches(path, t) for t in opts.type_exclude):
        return False
    return True

def display_for(root: str, rel: str, explicit_root: str, is_default: bool) -> str:
    relp = rel.replace(os.sep, "/")
    if relp == ".":
        relp = os.path.basename(root)
    if os.path.isfile(root):
        return explicit_root
    if explicit_root in (".", "./") or explicit_root.startswith("./"):
        return "./" + relp if relp else "./"
    if is_default:
        return relp
    prefix = explicit_root.rstrip("/")
    return (prefix + "/" + relp) if relp else explicit_root

def iter_files_for_root(root_arg: str, opts: Options, is_default: bool=False) -> Iterator[tuple[str, str]]:
    if root_arg == "-":
        yield "-", "-"; return
    root = root_arg
    if not os.path.exists(root):
        raise FileNotFoundError(root)
    ignore_pats = ignore_patterns_for_root(root, opts)
    if os.path.isfile(root):
        disp = root_arg
        rel = os.path.basename(root)
        if opts.max_filesize is not None:
            try:
                if os.path.getsize(root) > opts.max_filesize:
                    return
            except OSError:
                pass
        if passes_globs(disp, rel, opts) and passes_type(root, opts):
            yield root, disp
        return
    base = root
    # stack-based traversal; reverse scandir entries gives output close to rg's walk in many cases.
    stack: list[tuple[str, int]] = [(base, 0)]
    while stack:
        d, depth = stack.pop()
        try:
            entries = list(os.scandir(d))
        except OSError as e:
            eprint(f"rg: {d}: IO error for operation on {d}: {e.strerror} (os error {e.errno})", opts)
            continue
        dirs = []
        files = []
        for ent in entries:
            rel = os.path.relpath(ent.path, base)
            if rel == ".": rel = ent.name
            rel_slash = rel.replace(os.sep, "/")
            try:
                isdir = ent.is_dir(follow_symlinks=opts.follow)
                isfile = ent.is_file(follow_symlinks=opts.follow)
            except OSError:
                continue
            # Hidden directories and files.
            if not opts.hidden and is_hidden_path(rel_slash):
                continue
            if match_gitignore(rel_slash, isdir, ignore_pats):
                continue
            if isdir:
                if opts.max_depth is None or depth + 1 < opts.max_depth:
                    dirs.append(ent.path)
            elif isfile:
                disp = display_for(base, rel, root_arg, is_default)
                if opts.max_filesize is not None:
                    try:
                        if ent.stat(follow_symlinks=opts.follow).st_size > opts.max_filesize:
                            continue
                    except OSError:
                        continue
                if passes_globs(disp, rel_slash, opts) and passes_type(ent.path, opts):
                    files.append((ent.path, disp))
        # Files before descending, with reverse-ish natural order like ripgrep's parallel walker often shows.
        for f in reversed(files):
            yield f
        for dd in dirs:
            stack.append((dd, depth + 1))

def gather_files(opts: Options) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    roots = opts.paths or ["."]
    out: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    default = (roots == ["."] and not opts.files)
    for r in roots:
        try:
            out.extend(list(iter_files_for_root(r, opts, is_default=default)))
        except FileNotFoundError:
            eprint(f"rg: {r}: IO error for operation on {r}: No such file or directory (os error 2)", opts)
            raise
    sortkey = opts.sort or ("path" if False else None)
    reverse = False
    if opts.sortr:
        sortkey = opts.sortr; reverse = True
    if sortkey or opts.sort == "path":
        if sortkey in ("path", "none", None):
            out.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=reverse)
        elif sortkey in ("modified", "accessed", "created"):
            idx = {"modified":"st_mtime", "accessed":"st_atime", "created":"st_ctime"}[sortkey]
            out.sort(key=lambda x: getattr(os.stat(x[0]), idx, 0), reverse=reverse)
        else:
            out.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=reverse)
    return out

# ---------- reading/searching/printing ----------

def decode_bytes(data: bytes, opts: Options) -> str:
    enc = opts.encoding.lower()
    if enc in ("none", "auto", ""):
        if data.startswith(b"\xff\xfe") or data.startswith(b"\xfe\xff"):
            try:
                return data.decode("utf-16")
            except UnicodeDecodeError:
                pass
        if data.startswith(b"\xef\xbb\xbf"):
            try:
                return data.decode("utf-8-sig", errors="replace")
            except Exception:
                pass
        return data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    aliases = {"latin-1":"latin1", "utf-16le":"utf-16le", "utf-16be":"utf-16be"}
    try:
        return data.decode(aliases.get(enc, enc), errors="replace")
    except LookupError:
        return data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

def read_file(path: str, opts: Options) -> bytes:
    if path == "-":
        return sys.stdin.buffer.read()
    if opts.pre:
        try:
            cp = subprocess.run([opts.pre, path], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
            return cp.stdout
        except Exception:
            pass
    if opts.search_zip:
        low = path.lower()
        try:
            if low.endswith((".gz", ".tgz")):
                with gzip.open(path, "rb") as f: return f.read()
            if low.endswith(".bz2"):
                with bz2.open(path, "rb") as f: return f.read()
            if low.endswith((".xz", ".lzma")):
                with lzma.open(path, "rb") as f: return f.read()
        except Exception:
            pass
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        return f.read()

def split_lines_keep(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
    # Return (line_without_final_newline, byte-ish char offset). Keep embedded NULs.
    lines: list[tuple[str, int]] = []
    off = 0
    for part in text.splitlines(True):
        raw = part
        line = raw[:-1] if raw.endswith("\n") else raw
        if line.endswith("\r"):
            line = line[:-1]
        lines.append((line, off))
        off += len(raw.encode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
    if text == "":
        return []
    if not text.endswith(("\n", "\r")):
        # splitlines(True) already included last line.
        pass
    return lines

def format_replacement(template: str, m: re.Match) -> str:
    out = ""
    i = 0
    while i < len(template):
        c = template[i]
        if c == "$" and i + 1 < len(template):
            j = i + 1
            if template[j] == "$":
                out += "$"; i += 2; continue
            if template[j] == "0":
                out += m.group(0); i += 2; continue
            if template[j].isdigit():
                k = j
                while k < len(template) and template[k].isdigit(): k += 1
                try:
                    out += m.group(int(template[j:k])) or ""
                except Exception:
                    pass
                i = k; continue
            if template[j] == "{":
                k = template.find("}", j+1)
                if k != -1:
                    name = template[j+1:k]
                    try:
                        out += m.group(name) or ""
                    except Exception:
                        pass
                    i = k+1; continue
        out += c; i += 1
    return out

def replace_line(line: str, regex, opts: Options) -> str:
    if opts.replace is None:
        return line
    return regex.sub(lambda m: format_replacement(opts.replace or "", m), line)

def colorize_line(line: str, regex, opts: Options) -> str:
    use = opts.color == "always" or (opts.color == "auto" and sys.stdout.isatty())
    if not use or opts.invert:
        return line
    return regex.sub(lambda m: "\x1b[0m\x1b[1m\x1b[31m" + m.group(0) + "\x1b[0m", line)

def c_path(path: str, opts: Options) -> str:
    if opts.path_separator and opts.path_separator != "/":
        path = path.replace("/", opts.path_separator)
    if opts.color == "always":
        return "\x1b[0m\x1b[35m" + path + "\x1b[0m"
    return path

def c_num(n: int | str, opts: Options) -> str:
    if opts.color == "always":
        return "\x1b[0m\x1b[32m" + str(n) + "\x1b[0m"
    return str(n)

def should_with_filename(opts: Options, nfiles: int, path: str) -> bool:
    if opts.with_filename is not None:
        return opts.with_filename
    return path != "-" and nfiles > 1

def should_line_number(opts: Options) -> bool:
    return bool(opts.line_number)

def print_out(s: str, stats: Stats):
    if not s.endswith("\n"):
        s += "\n"
    stats.bytes_printed += len(s.encode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
    sys.stdout.write(s)

def prefix_fields(path: str, lineno: int, col: Optional[int], byteoff: Optional[int], opts: Options, nfiles: int, context: bool=False) -> str:
    sep = opts.field_context_separator if context else opts.field_match_separator
    fields: list[str] = []
    if should_with_filename(opts, nfiles, path):
        fields.append(c_path(path, opts))
    if should_line_number(opts) or opts.vimgrep:
        fields.append(c_num(lineno, opts))
    if opts.column or opts.vimgrep:
        fields.append(c_num(col if col is not None else 1, opts))
    if opts.byte_offset:
        fields.append(c_num(byteoff if byteoff is not None else 0, opts))
    if not fields:
        return ""
    return sep.join(str(f) for f in fields) + sep

def line_matches(line: str, regex, opts: Options) -> tuple[bool, list[re.Match]]:
    ms = list(regex.finditer(line))
    matched = bool(ms)
    if opts.invert:
        return (not matched), []
    return matched, ms

def binary_message(path: str, nfiles: int, nuloff: int, opts: Options, stats: Stats):
    prefix = ""
    if should_with_filename(opts, nfiles, path):
        prefix = c_path(path, opts) + opts.field_match_separator + " "
    print_out(f'{prefix}binary file matches (found "\\0" byte around offset {nuloff})', stats)

def json_line(obj: dict, stats: Stats):
    s = json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
    print_out(s, stats)

def search_one(path: str, disp: str, data: bytes, regex, opts: Options, stats: Stats, nfiles: int) -> bool:
    stats.searches += 1
    stats.bytes_searched += len(data)
    nuloff = data.find(b"\0")
    text = decode_bytes(data, opts)
    lines = split_lines_keep(text)
    has_binary = nuloff >= 0 and not opts.text
    # Find matches first for modes that need whole-file counts/context.
    records = []  # dicts: line, lineno, off, matches, matched
    matched_lines_count = 0
    total_matches = 0
    for idx, (line, off) in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        matched, ms = line_matches(line, regex, opts)
        if opts.passthru and not matched:
            pass
        if matched:
            matched_lines_count += 1
            total_matches += max(1 if opts.invert else 0, len(ms))
            records.append({"idx": idx-1, "lineno": idx, "line": line, "off": off, "matches": ms, "matched": True})
            if opts.max_count is not None and matched_lines_count >= opts.max_count:
                # ripgrep stops after this many matching lines per file.
                break
    file_has_match = matched_lines_count > 0
    if file_has_match:
        stats.searches_with_match += 1
        stats.any_match = True
        stats.matched_lines += matched_lines_count
        stats.matches += total_matches
    if opts.quiet:
        return file_has_match
    if opts.json:
        json_line({"type":"begin","data":{"path":{"text":disp}}}, stats)
        for r in records:
            line = r["line"]
            full_line = line + "\n"
            subs = []
            for m in r["matches"]:
                subs.append({"match":{"text":m.group(0)},"start":m.start(),"end":m.end()})
            json_line({"type":"match","data":{"path":{"text":disp},"lines":{"text":full_line},"line_number":r["lineno"],"absolute_offset":r["off"],"submatches":subs}}, stats)
        json_line({"type":"end","data":{"path":{"text":disp},"binary_offset":None,"stats":{"elapsed":{"secs":0,"nanos":0,"human":"0.000000s"},"searches":1,"searches_with_match":1 if file_has_match else 0,"bytes_searched":len(data),"bytes_printed":0,"matched_lines":matched_lines_count,"matches":total_matches}}}, stats)
        return file_has_match
    if opts.count or opts.count_matches:
        val = total_matches if opts.count_matches else matched_lines_count
        if file_has_match or opts.include_zero or nfiles > 1:
            prefix = ""
            if should_with_filename(opts, nfiles, disp):
                prefix = c_path(disp, opts) + opts.field_match_separator
            print_out(f"{prefix}{val}", stats)
        return file_has_match
    if opts.files_with_matches:
        if file_has_match:
            sys.stdout.write(disp + ("\0" if opts.null else "\n")); stats.bytes_printed += len(disp)+1
        return file_has_match
    if opts.files_without_match:
        if not file_has_match:
            sys.stdout.write(disp + ("\0" if opts.null else "\n")); stats.bytes_printed += len(disp)+1
        return file_has_match
    if has_binary and file_has_match:
        binary_message(disp, nfiles, nuloff, opts, stats)
        return True
    if not file_has_match and not opts.passthru:
        return False
    # Context output: build set of line indices to print.
    matched_indices = {r["idx"] for r in records}
    to_print: dict[int, bool] = {}
    if opts.passthru:
        for i in range(len(lines)):
            to_print[i] = i in matched_indices
    else:
        for mi in matched_indices:
            for j in range(max(0, mi - opts.before), min(len(lines), mi + opts.after + 1)):
                to_print[j] = j in matched_indices
    # Heading groups.
    if opts.heading and should_with_filename(opts, nfiles, disp):
        print_out(c_path(disp, opts), stats)
    printed_any = False
    last_i: Optional[int] = None
    for i in sorted(to_print):
        if last_i is not None and i > last_i + 1 and (opts.before or opts.after) and not opts.heading:
            print_out(opts.context_separator, stats)
        line, off = lines[i]
        ismatch = to_print[i]
        lineno = i + 1
        matched, ms = line_matches(line, regex, opts)
        if opts.max_columns is not None and len(line) > opts.max_columns and not opts.max_columns_preview:
            line_to_show = f"[Omitted long line with {len(line)} columns]"
        else:
            line_to_show = line.lstrip() if opts.trim else line
        if opts.only_matching and ismatch and not opts.invert:
            for m in ms:
